symptom: playback differed on every host since before the cross-platform work (ledger 2026-10-03: 'Recording file may be corrupted' at 74be317 too); matrix 2026-10-05: playback differs on all nine hosts (milestones, progress)
cause: tools/app_e2e.py copies downloads/NTSD_2.4_2.0a/NTSD 2.4_2.0a/recording/20260331_012329_VS.lfr, which is tracked in Git LFS; this working tree holds the 130-byte pointer (oid sha256:37d56900c4955b8c31b8266351907562d3343832c037c9ef28b81adf1c0f6742, size 10867), not the recording. The game's loader (OriginalReplayFileInput, 43e620) treats a file under 1000 bytes as unreadable and shows the original 'Loading error!  Recording file may be corrupted!!' alert. 1,959 LFS files in the working tree are pointers; the recording's object is in the local LFS store.
fix: recording_bytes() in tools/app_e2e.py: when the file is an LFS pointer, read the object from <git-common-dir>/lfs/objects and check its SHA-256 and size against the pointer. No asset, reference or expected value changes; the working tree is untouched.

results.other hosts: not rerun yet (the matrix uses the same harness)

side effect noticed and undone: running git-lfs commands (ls-files/env/smudge) during the investigation installed post-checkout and pre-push hooks into core.hooksPath (.githooks); both untracked files were removed, and the harness reads the store directly so it never runs git-lfs
